Q: How to cache get_queryset() when using ForeignKeyWidget A:

I have tested this using the bulk_import script.

My view is that the QuerySet cache is being used and although you see the SELECT SQL output for the relation table, the cache is being used, therefore the performance hit is minimal.

I can see in my logs that the lookup on the FK table takes negligible time, even when importing 100k rows.

I also see that the cache breakpoint is being hit during import.

If you are seeing a slow import, then there must be something else going on, so it would be useful to understand what the issue is.

Please do your own testing but my view is that the Django QuerySet cache is working correctly and there should be no need to implement your own caching. I'll update the documentation.

Update

As Bohdan points out, this is not correct.

Even if you override get_queryset() to reuse the same QuerySet, the widget’s clean() method will still call .get() per row — so you may still incur one SQL query per row. In other words, caching the QuerySet alone doesn’t guarantee reduced DB load.

Q: Build failure in flutter awesome_notifications due to android receiver A:

Documentation is misleading.

Replace this line:

 <receiver android:name="me.carda.awesome_notifications.core.broadcasters.receivers.RefreshSchedulesReceiver" android:exported="true">

With this and it should work fine:

        <receiver android:name="me.carda.awesome_notifications.DartRefreshSchedulesReceiver" android:exported="true">

Q: How to configure pytest for alembic migrations A:

First, let's initializing the alembic and configure itself. (I prefer to place migrations for a project in a folder with the same name.)

alembic init app/migrations

After... open alembic.ini check and edit the following lines:

# .....
script_location = %(here)s/app/migrations  # <--- should be with %(here)s

# .....
sqlalchemy.url = # <--- uncomment this line and set empty

After... open the env.py file, that will be located in the app/migrations folder, and add the following code:

# include the configuration from the FastAPI app
from app.core.config import get_settings
settings = get_settings()

'''
Here we set the dynamic database URL.
If we use tests, we will substitute the value we need into sqlalchemy.url
(more on this below).
'''
DATABASE_URL = config.get_main_option('sqlalchemy.url') or settings.ALEMBIC_DATABASE_URL

If we work with our application, then the ALEMBIC_DATABASE_URL specified in our configuration file will be automatically taken.

This completes the alembic settings!

Now open .env file your project and add into some as:

ALEMBIC_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+psycopg2://user:password@127.0.0.1:5432/your_db
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://test:test@127.0.0.1:5434/test_db # 'sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:'

I deploy two postgres databases in Podman based on a single image of postgres version 18. For the main database, I specified port 5432 on the local machine and in the container (default postgres port). For the test database, I set the connection port to 5434, and in the container also left, the port 5432, as the containers are isolated from each other.

Here's an important! Alembic doesn't support asynchronous connections, so we use the psycopg2 adapter for standard migrations. The application must run asynchrone with database. For tests to run correctly, they must also run asynchronously. That's why, we use the asyncpg adapter for both the main and test databases.

Now, to run the tests, we need to create them and configure them. To do this, create the following structure in the project folder:

+---tests
|   |   conftest.py
|   |   pytest.ini
|   |   __init__.py
|   |
|   +---integration
|   |   \---crud
|   |       |   test_<name>.py
|   |
|   +---unit
|   |   \---services

Add the following code to conftest.py:

import pytest_asyncio

from typing import AsyncGenerator

from alembic import command
from alembic.config import Config

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine, AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker, create_async_engine
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool

from app.core.config import get_settings

settings = get_settings()


@pytest_asyncio.fixture(scope='session')
async def engine() -> AsyncGenerator[AsyncEngine, None]:
    # https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncEngine
    engine = create_async_engine(settings.TEST_DATABASE_URL, echo=False, poolclass=NullPool)
    yield engine
    await engine.dispose()


@pytest_asyncio.fixture
async def async_session(engine: AsyncEngine) -> AsyncGenerator[AsyncSession, None]:
    # https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.async_sessionmaker
    async with async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)() as session:
        async with session.begin():
            yield session


@pytest_asyncio.fixture(scope='session', autouse=True)
async def apply_migrations(engine: AsyncEngine) -> None:
    alembic_cfg = Config('alembic.ini')
    alembic_cfg.set_main_option('sqlalchemy.url', settings.TEST_DATABASE_URL)

    async with engine.connect() as connect:
        try:
            await connect.run_sync(lambda connection: command.upgrade(alembic_cfg, 'head'))
            # https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/orm/extensions/asyncio.html#sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio.AsyncConnection.run_sync
            # await connect.run_sync(lambda sync_conn: command.downgrade(alembic_cfg, 'base'))  # optional
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error applying migrations: {e}")
            raise
        finally:
            await connect.rollback()

Explanations:

  • Each test started with a clean database. All changes made during the test disappeared after its completion. Even if the test failed mid-run, the database didn't remain "dirty."

    with session.begin()

  • Replace the database URL. Since SQLAlchemy hide the password when outputting the URL, we explicitly use the database URL from .env, and not, for example, from engine.url, i.e., we essentially transfer raw data:

    alembic_cfg.set_main_option('sqlalchemy.url', settings.TEST_DATABASE_URL)

Important!

  • Use run_sync for synchronous migrations, since Alembic itself is not asynchronous.

  • Create one asynchronous engine for the entire test session using parameter scope='session' of fixture.

  • Create an asynchronous SQLAlchemy session for each test a fixture as function, as tests must be isolated so that changes to the database in one test do not affect others.

    If you set scope='session', all tests will use the same session object, which can lead to conflicts.

  • Since migrations need to be run once for the entire test session, and not before each test and for automatically upgrade migrations before tests, also using the scope='session' for fixture and option autouse=True.

  • For the migration fixture to run, there must be at least one active integration test associated with the database!

As a result, running the pytest test command will now automatically apply migrations to the database.

Also, when running migrations in the normal Alembic mode, the migrations will be applied to the main database without affecting the test database.

Tested on: alembic==1.17.2, fastapi==0.124.0, pytest==9.0.2, SQLAlchemy==2.0.44, PG_VERSION=18.0-1.pgdg13+3 (Podman systemd units)

Q: HTTP ERROR 403 No valid crumb was included in the request error with GitLab+Jenkins on windows environment A:

You don't need to reconfigure your Jenkins instance. What you should do is the following:

  1. Go to the Jenkins project you want to use;
  2. Go to Configure -> Build triggers section;
  3. See the name of the checkbox Build when a change is pushed to GitLab. GitLab webhook URL: <TARGET URL>

What you're looking for is the "TARGET URL" from step 3. See the screenshot for an example of such an URL. As you can see it has the needed project format:

Q: IllegalArgumentException: reportSizeConfigurations: ActivityRecord not found for: Token A:

The main problem should be that the app is stuck and the user is impatient and returns to the launcher. However, the original app code obtains the time slice to run at this time. There are quite a few users reporting this issue on issuetracker. You should focus on monitoring app lags. In fact, this is information provided by a comment on issuetracker, but I can't find it for the time being.
